title: PostgreSQL unavailable after Linux server restart
description: The internal application cannot connect to PostgreSQL after the database server was restarted.
error_message: connection to server at "db-server-01", port 5432 failed: Connection refused
symptoms: Application login fails; server responds to ping; port 5432 is not accepting connections.
technician_notes: Checked the PostgreSQL service with systemctl and reviewed the service logs.
root_cause: An invalid PostgreSQL configuration prevented the database service from starting.
solution: Corrected the configuration, restarted PostgreSQL, verified port 5432, and tested application connectivity.

title: Application connection refused on PostgreSQL port
description: The reporting application stopped reaching its database after routine maintenance on the database host.
error_message: psycopg2.OperationalError: could not connect to server: Connection refused
symptoms: Reports fail to load; database host is reachable; PostgreSQL process is absent.
technician_notes: Compared service status with the last maintenance record and checked the PostgreSQL startup log.
root_cause: The PostgreSQL service was disabled during a package maintenance operation.
solution: Enabled and started the PostgreSQL service, then reran the application database health check.

title: Database service failed after configuration change
description: A web application reports database errors after a change to the PostgreSQL listener settings.
error_message: FATAL: could not create any TCP/IP sockets
symptoms: The application cannot authenticate; local PostgreSQL checks also fail; the service enters failed state.
technician_notes: Validated postgresql.conf syntax and inspected systemd journal entries.
root_cause: The configured listen address was invalid for the database host.
solution: Restored a valid listen address, started the service, and verified local and application connections.

title: PostgreSQL not listening after server reboot
description: The inventory service cannot reach its PostgreSQL database following an overnight server restart.
error_message: connection to server at 10.0.20.15, port 5432 failed: Connection refused
symptoms: Inventory requests time out; host is online; netstat shows no listener on port 5432.
technician_notes: Inspected service dependencies and checked the database error log after boot.
root_cause: A failed filesystem check delayed a database dependency and PostgreSQL did not start.
solution: Resolved the filesystem check issue, started PostgreSQL, and confirmed inventory requests completed normally.

title: PostgreSQL rejects application connections
description: The application reaches the database host but new connections are rejected after a database restart.
error_message: FATAL: no pg_hba.conf entry for host 10.0.10.20
symptoms: Application health check reaches port 5432 but authentication fails for all users.
technician_notes: Reviewed pg_hba.conf entries and compared the application subnet with the allowed networks.
root_cause: The application subnet was missing from the PostgreSQL client authentication rules.
solution: Added the approved private subnet rule, reloaded PostgreSQL, and tested an application connection.

title: Internal hostname resolution stopped working
description: Several internal applications cannot resolve service hostnames while direct private IP connections still work.
symptoms: Pings to private IPs succeed; hostnames fail; multiple services report DNS lookup errors.
technician_notes: Used dig and resolvectl to compare configured resolvers and checked the DNS service status.
root_cause: The resolver configuration pointed to an unreachable DNS server.
solution: Restored the approved internal resolver, flushed the resolver cache, and confirmed hostname lookups.

title: DNS timeout after network configuration change
description: A Linux workstation and its development tools cannot resolve internal domains after a network profile update.
symptoms: Internal websites do not open; public websites resolve; DNS queries to the configured server time out.
technician_notes: Compared the active NetworkManager profile with the standard workstation profile.
root_cause: A manual network profile change replaced the internal DNS address with an unavailable example address.
solution: Applied the standard network profile and verified internal and public DNS resolution.

title: Application cannot resolve database hostname
description: The service is healthy locally but cannot start because the configured database hostname is not resolved.
error_message: socket.gaierror: [Errno -2] Name or service not known
symptoms: Application startup retries database connection; database IP is reachable directly; hostname lookup fails.
technician_notes: Checked application environment variables and tested the database name with getent hosts.
root_cause: The database hostname had a spelling error in the application environment configuration.
solution: Corrected the hostname, restarted the application service, and confirmed the database health check.

title: DNS record missing for internal web service
description: Users receive an unknown host error when opening the new internal web service name.
symptoms: The web server responds by private IP but the service name returns NXDOMAIN from internal clients.
technician_notes: Queried the authoritative internal DNS zone and reviewed the deployment request.
root_cause: The DNS A record was not added when the web service was provisioned.
solution: Added the approved internal A record, reloaded DNS, and verified resolution from two client networks.

title: No space left on Linux root filesystem
description: A Linux application server reports write failures and the service begins returning errors.
symptoms: Application cannot create files; df reports 100% usage on /; SSH login is slow.
technician_notes: Used df and du to locate large rotated logs and checked for deleted files held open by processes.
root_cause: Unmanaged application logs filled the root filesystem.
solution: Archived and removed approved old logs, configured log rotation, and verified filesystem capacity and service recovery.

title: Application cannot write logs because disk is full
description: The order service is running but cannot record new events after its server storage reached capacity.
error_message: java.io.IOException: No space left on device
symptoms: New requests intermittently fail; log files stop growing; the application log partition is at 100%.
technician_notes: Checked filesystem utilization and found oversized debug logs from a temporary verbose setting.
root_cause: Debug logging generated more data than the application volume could hold.
solution: Removed old debug logs, restored normal logging, increased the volume allocation, and verified new log writes.

title: Docker stopped when var partition reached capacity
description: Several containers stopped unexpectedly on a host whose Docker data partition is full.
error_message: failed to register layer: no space left on device
symptoms: Containers cannot restart; /var/lib/docker is full; Docker commands take longer than usual.
technician_notes: Measured Docker image and container log usage and identified unused old images.
root_cause: Unused Docker images and unbounded container logs consumed the Docker partition.
solution: Removed approved unused images, limited container log retention, and restarted affected containers.

title: Database cannot create temporary files
description: Analytical queries fail because PostgreSQL cannot create temporary files on the database host.
error_message: could not write to file "base/pgsql_tmp": No space left on device
symptoms: Small queries work; reporting queries fail; database temporary storage is full.
technician_notes: Reviewed filesystem usage and active query temporary file settings during a low-traffic period.
root_cause: A reporting job created unusually large temporary files on a nearly full volume.
solution: Stopped the stuck report, cleared approved temporary files, and scheduled the report with a resource limit.

title: Nginx returns 502 Bad Gateway
description: The internal website returns a 502 response after the application service was redeployed.
symptoms: Nginx is reachable; every proxied request returns 502; the application process is not listening on port 8000.
technician_notes: Checked Nginx error logs, upstream configuration, and the application systemd service status.
root_cause: The application service failed during deployment and the configured upstream port had no listener.
solution: Fixed the application startup error, restarted the service, and verified Nginx proxy requests.

title: Website returns HTTP 503 after deployment
description: The customer portal shows HTTP 503 responses immediately after a release deployment.
symptoms: Web server answers requests but marks the backend unavailable; health endpoint fails after release.
technician_notes: Reviewed reverse proxy logs and compared the release environment variables with the previous version.
root_cause: The deployed application was listening on a different port than the proxy configuration expected.
solution: Updated the proxy target to the application port, restarted Apache, and completed a smoke test.

title: Nginx upstream connection refused
description: Requests to a web service fail through Nginx while the reverse proxy process itself remains healthy.
error_message: connect() failed (111: Connection refused) while connecting to upstream
symptoms: Nginx status is active; backend URL is unavailable locally; browser receives 502.
technician_notes: Tested the upstream port with curl and reviewed the Java service journal.
root_cause: The backend service stopped after an out-of-memory termination.
solution: Adjusted the service memory setting, restarted the backend, and confirmed stable proxy responses.

title: Apache serves default page instead of application
description: The application domain displays the web server default page after a virtual host update.
error_message: HTTP 200 with Apache2 Debian Default Page
symptoms: Web server responds normally but the expected application content is not displayed for the internal hostname.
technician_notes: Listed enabled virtual hosts and checked the Host header mapping.
root_cause: The intended virtual host was not enabled after the configuration change.
solution: Enabled the correct virtual host, reloaded Apache, and verified the application hostname.

title: Docker container repeatedly restarts
description: The API container enters a restart loop after a new image was deployed to the development host.
symptoms: Container status alternates between restarting and exited; API port is unavailable; logs show startup failure.
technician_notes: Inspected docker compose logs and compared the image command with the previous release.
root_cause: The container command referenced a configuration file missing from the new image.
solution: Included the required configuration file in the image, rebuilt the service, and verified healthy container status.

title: Docker container exits with code 1
description: A worker container stops immediately after startup on the integration environment.
error_message: Error: required setting WORKER_QUEUE is not defined
symptoms: Worker container remains exited; dependent API requests queue indefinitely; container logs show a missing setting.
technician_notes: Reviewed compose environment entries and compared them with the service configuration reference.
root_cause: The deployment environment omitted a required worker queue variable.
solution: Added the missing non-sensitive environment setting and recreated the worker container.

title: Container cannot connect to database
description: The application container is running but its health check fails while connecting to the database service.
error_message: could not translate host name "localhost" to address
symptoms: API container is up; database container is healthy; API health check reports database unavailable.
technician_notes: Reviewed compose network membership and the database host in the API environment.
root_cause: The container used localhost instead of the database service name for its connection host.
solution: Changed the database host to the compose service name and recreated the API container.

title: Container fails because environment variable is missing
description: A scheduled processing container will not start after its compose definition was moved to another host.
symptoms: Container exits during initialization; the image is present; logs show a missing application mode variable.
technician_notes: Compared the host environment file with the approved compose example and checked variable interpolation.
root_cause: The environment file was not copied when the compose project moved hosts.
solution: Created the local environment file with non-secret settings and restarted the scheduled container.

title: Linux service fails to start after package update
description: A background Linux service is inactive following a routine operating system package update.
error_message: Job for telemetry-agent.service failed because the control process exited with error code
symptoms: Monitoring reports the agent offline; system is reachable; service status is failed after reboot.
technician_notes: Used systemctl status and journalctl to identify the failing post-update configuration directive.
root_cause: The package update removed a configuration option no longer supported by the agent version.
solution: Removed the obsolete option, validated the configuration, and restarted the service.

title: Linux server boot delayed by failed mount
description: A utility server becomes available slowly because a configured data mount is unavailable during boot.
error_message: Dependency failed for /srv/shared; timed out waiting for device
symptoms: Boot takes several minutes; services depending on /srv/shared remain inactive; virtual disk is healthy.
technician_notes: Reviewed fstab and systemd mount units and checked the device identifier.
root_cause: The fstab entry referenced an outdated virtual disk UUID.
solution: Updated the UUID with the current device identifier and rebooted to verify normal startup.

title: Scheduled Linux job did not run
description: A nightly maintenance script did not execute on the expected application server.
symptoms: Expected cleanup output is absent; manual script execution from the project directory succeeds.
technician_notes: Checked cron entries, working directory assumptions, and the job output log.
root_cause: The cron entry used a relative script path that was not valid from cron's working directory.
solution: Changed the entry to an absolute path and verified the next scheduled execution.

title: Windows workstation becomes unresponsive
description: A Windows workstation freezes during normal office use and requires a restart.
symptoms: Desktop freezes when opening large files; disk activity remains high; restart temporarily restores responsiveness.
technician_notes: Reviewed Reliability Monitor, startup programs, and available disk space.
root_cause: A failed update left a background indexing process repeatedly scanning a large temporary directory.
solution: Completed the pending update, cleared the temporary directory, and rebuilt the affected index.

title: Windows update repeatedly fails
description: A Windows 10 support workstation cannot complete its monthly update and reports an installation rollback.
error_message: 0x800f081f - The source files could not be found
symptoms: Update downloads successfully but rolls back during installation; user can continue working.
technician_notes: Checked update history and repaired the component store with the standard Windows servicing tools.
root_cause: Corrupted Windows component store files prevented the update from applying.
solution: Repaired the component store, cleared the update cache, and installed the update successfully.

title: Windows service fails after restart
description: A Windows-hosted internal service does not start automatically after the server reboots.
symptoms: IIS site is unavailable after reboot; starting the service manually fails with an access error.
technician_notes: Reviewed Windows event logs and the service logon account permissions on the application directory.
root_cause: The service account lost read and execute permission on the application directory.
solution: Restored the required directory permissions and restarted the service to verify automatic startup.

title: Windows workstation cannot access shared folder
description: A user cannot open an internal file share from a Windows workstation while internet access works.
symptoms: Other websites work; mapped drive shows disconnected; the file server hostname resolves successfully.
technician_notes: Tested the share path, reviewed cached credentials, and checked the user's group membership.
root_cause: The workstation retained an expired cached credential for the file share.
solution: Removed the stale credential, reauthenticated with the approved account, and remapped the share.

title: Users cannot reach internal application
description: Users on one office network cannot reach an internal application, while users on another network can connect normally.
symptoms: Ping is blocked; TCP connection times out only from one subnet; application host is healthy.
technician_notes: Compared routing tables and firewall policy counters for both office subnets.
root_cause: A network firewall rule omitted the source subnet after a rule reordering.
solution: Restored the approved inter-subnet rule and verified application access from both networks.

title: Intermittent packet loss to application server
description: Users report intermittent delays and disconnects when using an internal application.
error_message: Request timed out; 18% packet loss to 10.0.20.15
symptoms: Application sessions disconnect intermittently; packet loss appears from one switch segment; server metrics are normal.
technician_notes: Ran ping and traceroute from multiple segments and reviewed switch port error counters.
root_cause: A damaged network cable caused CRC errors on the access switch port.
solution: Replaced the cable, cleared the port errors, and confirmed stable latency and zero packet loss.

title: VPN clients cannot reach internal subnet
description: Remote users can establish VPN sessions but cannot connect to internal application addresses.
symptoms: VPN authentication succeeds; internal DNS works; connections to application servers fail from VPN clients.
technician_notes: Checked VPN route advertisements and compared the client route table with the approved remote access policy.
root_cause: The internal application subnet was missing from the VPN client route list.
solution: Added the subnet to the VPN route configuration and verified access with a test client.

title: Network interface loses link after reboot
description: A Linux server comes online without its secondary network interface after a kernel restart.
error_message: Could not bring up interface ens192
symptoms: Primary management access works; services on the secondary private interface are unreachable after reboot.
technician_notes: Inspected interface names with ip link and compared netplan configuration to the host hardware names.
root_cause: The netplan file referenced an interface name that changed after the kernel update.
solution: Updated the interface name in netplan, applied the configuration, and verified both interfaces.

title: User authentication fails after password reset
description: A user cannot sign in to an internal application after completing a password reset.
symptoms: Password reset succeeds in the directory portal; application login continues to reject the account; other users can log in.
technician_notes: Checked account status, authentication timestamps, and the application's directory synchronization logs.
root_cause: The application cached the old directory credential until its authentication service was refreshed.
solution: Refreshed the application authentication service and confirmed login with the new password.

title: Access denied to shared project directory
description: A development user receives permission errors when opening a shared project directory.
symptoms: User can access other shares; project share denies read and write access; group membership appears recently changed.
technician_notes: Compared effective share permissions with the user's directory groups and reviewed the access request.
root_cause: The user was removed from the approved project group during an account synchronization.
solution: Restored the approved group membership and verified read and write access to the share.

title: Linux service cannot read configuration file
description: An application service fails to start after a configuration file was replaced during maintenance.
symptoms: Service is failed; configuration syntax is valid; manual root inspection can read the file.
technician_notes: Checked file ownership, mode bits, and the service account configured in the unit file.
root_cause: The replacement configuration file was owned by root and unreadable by the service account.
solution: Set the approved ownership and permissions, restarted the service, and checked its health endpoint.

title: Application role missing required permission
description: A user can log in to the application but cannot open the reporting page.
symptoms: Authentication succeeds; dashboard opens; reporting page returns 403 only for one user's role.
technician_notes: Compared the user's application role with a peer account and reviewed the authorization audit entry.
root_cause: The user's role did not include the reporting permission after a team transfer.
solution: Applied the approved reporting role and verified access without changing authentication settings.

title: Web application responds slowly under normal load
description: Users report slow page loads during regular morning activity on the application server.
symptoms: CPU remains above 95%; request latency increases; database and network health remain normal.
technician_notes: Reviewed process CPU usage, application worker count, and recent deployment changes.
root_cause: A debug process spawned excessive worker processes and exhausted available CPU.
solution: Stopped the debug process, restored the standard worker count, and confirmed normal response times.

title: Linux server runs out of memory
description: An API host becomes intermittently unavailable when memory usage reaches capacity.
symptoms: API restarts unexpectedly; free memory reaches zero; kernel log reports an OOM kill.
technician_notes: Reviewed memory graphs, JVM heap configuration, and kernel messages around the restart time.
root_cause: The Java heap limit was set too close to total host memory, leaving no room for the operating system.
solution: Reduced the JVM heap limit, restarted the service, and monitored memory usage during normal traffic.

title: High CPU caused by stuck worker process
description: A background processing server reports high CPU and delayed jobs.
error_message: Load average above 12.0; worker heartbeat missed
symptoms: One worker consumes a full CPU core continuously; queued jobs grow; other workers remain healthy.
technician_notes: Inspected process stacks and worker logs and isolated a job retrying without backoff.
root_cause: A malformed input caused a worker retry loop with no delay.
solution: Stopped the affected worker, corrected retry handling in the deployed configuration, and drained the queue.

title: System performance degraded after log collector update
description: A server becomes slow shortly after a monitoring agent update.
symptoms: Interactive commands are delayed; the monitoring agent is the top CPU consumer; application workload is unchanged.
technician_notes: Compared agent configuration before and after update and checked its collection interval.
root_cause: The new agent configuration enabled an overly frequent filesystem scan.
solution: Restored the standard collection interval, restarted the agent, and verified host load returned to normal.

title: Deployment fails during application startup
description: The latest application release deploys successfully but fails its startup health check.
symptoms: Deployment pipeline completes; service exits immediately; previous application version was healthy.
technician_notes: Reviewed deployment logs, virtual environment contents, and dependency lock changes.
root_cause: The release dependency file omitted a package imported by the application.
solution: Added the missing dependency, rebuilt the deployment artifact, and passed the startup health check.

title: Release rollback caused by failed health check
description: An application release is automatically rolled back because the readiness endpoint does not become healthy.
symptoms: New instances start but are removed by deployment automation; logs show configuration validation errors.
technician_notes: Compared environment configuration between the old and new deployment manifests.
root_cause: A required non-secret feature setting was absent from the new deployment manifest.
solution: Added the missing setting, redeployed the version, and verified readiness and rollback checks.

title: Application deployment uses wrong configuration profile
description: The deployed application starts but connects to the wrong internal service profile.
symptoms: Application page loads; data operations fail; logs show a test database hostname in the staging environment.
technician_notes: Inspected release variables and deployment job parameters used for the affected environment.
root_cause: The deployment job selected the test configuration profile instead of the staging profile.
solution: Corrected the profile selection, redeployed, and verified database operations against the staging service.

title: Static assets missing after web deployment
description: The application page loads after deployment but styles and client-side assets return not found errors.
symptoms: HTML is served; browser console shows 404 for JavaScript and CSS files; API calls are unaffected.
technician_notes: Compared the build output directory with the Nginx static root and reviewed the deployment copy step.
root_cause: The deployment pipeline copied the HTML but skipped the generated static asset directory.
solution: Updated the copy step to include static assets, redeployed, and verified browser requests.

title: HTTP 404 for valid application route
description: A valid application route returns 404 through the reverse proxy after a routing change.
symptoms: Root page works; the reports route returns 404 through Nginx; direct application access exposes the route.
technician_notes: Compared Nginx location blocks with the application's route prefix and tested both proxy paths.
root_cause: The reverse proxy location removed the /api prefix before forwarding, producing an invalid backend path.
solution: Corrected the proxy path handling, reloaded Nginx, and verified the reports route.

title: HTTP 500 from malformed request handling
description: A web endpoint returns server errors for a subset of valid form submissions.
symptoms: Most requests work; submissions containing an optional field fail; application logs show a null value exception.
technician_notes: Reproduced the request with a sanitized test payload and reviewed the endpoint traceback.
root_cause: The handler assumed an optional request field was always present.
solution: Added validation for the optional field, deployed the patch, and tested valid and incomplete payloads.

title: HTTP request timeout on large report
description: Users receive a gateway timeout when exporting a large report from the internal web application.
symptoms: Small reports complete; large reports time out after one minute; database query continues running.
technician_notes: Reviewed proxy timeout settings and database query duration using a sanitized report filter.
root_cause: The report query lacked an index and exceeded the reverse proxy timeout.
solution: Added the approved database index and verified the report completed within the existing timeout.

title: PostgreSQL query performance degraded
description: A reporting application becomes slow when loading recently expanded data tables.
error_message: canceling statement due to statement timeout
symptoms: Simple queries succeed; reports exceed the statement timeout; database CPU increases during report execution.
technician_notes: Reviewed query plans and table statistics for the affected report query.
root_cause: A frequently filtered column lacked an index after a data model change.
solution: Added and analyzed the appropriate index, then verified query duration and report completion.

title: PostgreSQL database reports too many connections
description: The application intermittently fails to open database sessions during a busy period.
error_message: FATAL: sorry, too many clients already
symptoms: New application requests fail intermittently; active connection count reaches max_connections; idle sessions remain open.
technician_notes: Inspected PostgreSQL activity and application connection pool settings during the incident window.
root_cause: An application worker leak left idle database connections open.
solution: Recycled the affected workers, reduced idle pool retention, and verified connection counts returned to normal.

title: PostgreSQL backup job fails
description: The nightly PostgreSQL backup reports failure even though the database remains available.
error_message: pg_dump: error: connection to server failed: FATAL: password authentication failed
symptoms: Backup file is not created; application connections work; backup job logs show authentication failure.
technician_notes: Checked the backup role status and compared the scheduled job configuration with the approved service account settings.
root_cause: The backup job referenced an outdated non-secret connection setting after a role update.
solution: Updated the approved backup connection configuration and completed a test and scheduled backup.

title: Network DNS lookup fails for service endpoint
description: A monitoring probe cannot resolve an internal service endpoint even though the service host is online.
symptoms: Probe reports endpoint down; direct IP probe succeeds; repeated DNS queries return SERVFAIL.
technician_notes: Checked the zone serial, authoritative server response, and recent DNS configuration changes.
root_cause: A malformed zone record caused the authoritative DNS server to return SERVFAIL.
solution: Corrected the zone record, incremented the zone serial, and verified recursive lookups.

title: Linux package repository unavailable
description: A server cannot retrieve approved packages during a maintenance task.
symptoms: APT update fails; general network connectivity works; repository hostname cannot be resolved.
technician_notes: Tested repository hostname resolution and compared the APT source configuration with the standard server profile.
root_cause: The repository source contained an obsolete internal hostname.
solution: Updated the source to the current approved repository hostname and completed an APT update.

title: Windows print service unavailable
description: A Windows workstation cannot print to the internal test printer queue.
error_message: The Print Spooler service is not running
symptoms: Print jobs remain queued; printer is reachable from another workstation; local spooler is stopped.
technician_notes: Checked the spooler event log and cleared a corrupted pending print job.
root_cause: A malformed print job caused the local Print Spooler service to stop.
solution: Cleared the stuck job, restarted the Print Spooler, and printed a test page.

title: Web server certificate warning in browser
description: Users receive a certificate warning when accessing the internal service over HTTPS.
symptoms: HTTPS endpoint responds; browser warns that the certificate is expired; service certificate monitoring is alerting.
technician_notes: Checked certificate validity dates and the configured certificate path on the reverse proxy.
root_cause: The scheduled certificate replacement did not reload the reverse proxy with the renewed certificate.
solution: Installed the renewed certificate, reloaded Nginx, and verified the certificate dates from a client.

title: Service deployment blocked by file ownership
description: A deployment script cannot replace application files on the Linux web host.
error_message: cp: cannot create regular file '/opt/example-app/app.py': Permission denied
symptoms: Build succeeds; deployment stops while copying files; existing application version remains online.
technician_notes: Reviewed deployment account membership and ownership of the application directory.
root_cause: The deployment directory ownership was changed during manual maintenance.
solution: Restored the approved deployment group ownership and reran the deployment script.

title: Application cannot create upload directory
description: Users cannot upload documents because the application cannot create its upload directory.
symptoms: Existing downloads work; new uploads return HTTP 500; directory is present but owned by root.
technician_notes: Checked application service account and directory permissions without exposing uploaded content.
root_cause: The upload directory was recreated with ownership that excluded the application service account.
solution: Restored the approved directory ownership and permissions, then tested a harmless sample upload.

title: Docker health check fails on startup
description: A container remains unhealthy even though its process is running after deployment.
error_message: Healthcheck failed: curl: (7) Failed to connect to localhost port 8080
symptoms: Container process is running; orchestrated service is marked unhealthy; application listens on port 8000 inside the container.
technician_notes: Inspected the container health check and compared it with the application listen port.
root_cause: The health check used the old application port after a service configuration change.
solution: Updated the health check to the current internal port and recreated the container.

title: HTTP reverse proxy sends requests to wrong service
description: The web hostname returns an unexpected application response after a proxy configuration update.
symptoms: TLS and Nginx respond normally; hostname displays another service's 404 page; backend services are healthy.
technician_notes: Reviewed server_name precedence and the order of enabled Nginx site configurations.
root_cause: A duplicate server_name entry caused Nginx to select the wrong virtual host.
solution: Removed the duplicate host entry, reloaded Nginx, and verified the expected backend response.

title: Monitoring alert caused by stale service check
description: Monitoring reports an application outage although users can access the service normally.
symptoms: Users reach the application; monitoring shows down; endpoint now redirects HTTP to HTTPS.
technician_notes: Compared the monitor request path and status expectation with the current web server behavior.
root_cause: The monitor was not updated after the service began enforcing HTTPS redirects.
solution: Updated the check to use HTTPS and the expected redirect-free health endpoint.

title: Disk usage alert on application log volume
description: Monitoring warns that the application log volume is nearing capacity on a production-like test host.
symptoms: Application is healthy; disk alert threshold is exceeded; recent deployment generated larger logs than usual.
technician_notes: Reviewed directory sizes and log retention settings and confirmed no deleted files were held open.
root_cause: A temporary verbose deployment setting increased log volume growth.
solution: Restored normal logging, compressed eligible logs, and verified usage returned below the alert threshold.

title: Database hostname changed after environment refresh
description: A refreshed application environment fails database connectivity because its configured service name is outdated.
error_message: could not translate host name "old-db-server" to address
symptoms: Application starts but all database operations fail; current database host responds to ping; old hostname does not resolve.
technician_notes: Compared environment variables with the refreshed environment inventory and tested current service DNS.
root_cause: The environment refresh changed the database hostname without updating the application configuration.
solution: Updated the database hostname, restarted the application, and verified read and write operations.

title: Internal API unavailable after firewall update
description: A service-to-service API call fails after a network firewall policy update.
error_message: curl: (28) Connection timed out after 5000 milliseconds
symptoms: Frontend service is healthy; backend API is healthy locally; calls across the service subnet time out.
technician_notes: Checked firewall change history and compared permitted source and destination ports.
root_cause: The firewall update removed the approved HTTPS rule between the two private service subnets.
solution: Restored the specific private-subnet HTTPS rule and verified the service-to-service request.

title: Windows application crashes on startup
description: A Windows utility closes immediately when a user launches it after a workstation update.
symptoms: Application window does not open; other applications work; Windows event log reports a missing runtime component.
technician_notes: Reviewed the application event entry and compared installed runtime versions with the supported application version.
root_cause: A required desktop runtime was removed during workstation cleanup.
solution: Installed the approved runtime package and verified the application launched successfully.

title: Linux disk mount is read-only
description: An application cannot update files because its data filesystem has remounted as read-only.
symptoms: Application reads existing data but cannot write updates; dmesg reports filesystem I/O errors.
technician_notes: Checked mount state and kernel messages, then followed the approved maintenance procedure for filesystem checks.
root_cause: Filesystem errors caused the kernel to remount the data volume read-only.
solution: Placed the service in maintenance, repaired the filesystem during reboot, remounted it read-write, and verified writes.

title: Application deployment leaves old version active
description: A release pipeline reports success but users continue to receive the previous application version.
symptoms: Deployment job is green; server files contain the new build; running service still reports the old version.
technician_notes: Checked deployment service reload behavior and compared the running process start time with the release timestamp.
root_cause: The pipeline copied the new files but did not restart the systemd service.
solution: Added the service restart to the deployment step, deployed again, and verified the version endpoint.

title: Slow DNS resolution on application host
description: An application experiences delayed startup because DNS queries from its host take several seconds.
symptoms: Application startup is slow; direct IP connections are fast; repeated hostname queries show intermittent delay.
technician_notes: Measured resolver response times and reviewed resolver order and retry behavior.
root_cause: The first configured DNS resolver was reachable but responded slowly to internal names.
solution: Placed the approved internal resolver first, flushed the cache, and confirmed normal lookup latency.

title: Database backup storage is nearly full
description: The database backup host warns that available storage is below the operational threshold.
symptoms: Nightly backups still complete; oldest backup files exceed the retention period; monitoring warns of imminent capacity exhaustion.
technician_notes: Reviewed backup sizes and retention timestamps without opening any sensitive backup contents.
root_cause: The retention cleanup task stopped running after a scheduler configuration change.
solution: Ran the approved cleanup, restored the scheduled task, and verified the backup volume and next run.

title: Nginx configuration reload fails
description: A reverse proxy configuration change cannot be applied because Nginx rejects the updated file.
symptoms: Existing site remains available; configuration reload fails; new proxy setting is not active.
technician_notes: Ran nginx -t and reviewed the changed site configuration against the documented directive names.
root_cause: A misspelled Nginx directive made the configuration invalid.
solution: Corrected the directive spelling, validated the configuration, and reloaded Nginx successfully.

title: Docker image pull fails on build host
description: A build host cannot pull an approved base image for a local application build.
error_message: failed to resolve source metadata: network timeout
symptoms: Existing containers run; new builds fail during image metadata retrieval; registry hostname resolves intermittently.
technician_notes: Tested registry DNS and HTTPS connectivity and reviewed Docker daemon proxy settings.
root_cause: The Docker daemon was using an outdated proxy address after the network change.
solution: Updated the daemon proxy configuration, restarted Docker, and completed a test image pull.

title: Application login page returns 401
description: The application login page is available but rejects valid test user authentication after a service update.
symptoms: Login form loads; all test users receive 401; directory service is reachable; application logs show an authentication bind error.
technician_notes: Checked the authentication service configuration and compared the directory endpoint with the approved environment settings.
root_cause: The application authentication endpoint was changed during a service update but the client configuration was not updated.
solution: Updated the approved directory endpoint, restarted the authentication component, and verified test logins.

title: Application health check reports database timeout
description: The service health endpoint reports a database timeout while the database server remains reachable.
error_message: HTTP 503: database health check timed out
symptoms: Web pages load intermittently; health endpoint fails; direct database port test succeeds; connection pool is exhausted.
technician_notes: Reviewed health endpoint logs and database connection pool utilization during the alert.
root_cause: A batch task retained database connections longer than expected and exhausted the application's pool.
solution: Stopped the stuck batch task, released connections, and applied the approved pool timeout setting.

title: Linux host clock is out of sync
description: Authentication and monitoring events on a Linux host show timestamps several minutes behind the rest of the environment.
symptoms: Logs have inconsistent timestamps; time-sensitive authentication checks fail; host reports no active time source.
technician_notes: Checked timedatectl, chrony sources, and outbound access to the approved time service.
root_cause: The time synchronization service was disabled after a package update.
solution: Enabled chrony, restored the approved time source, and verified the system clock synchronized.

title: Web application session expires immediately
description: Users can authenticate but are returned to the login page immediately after signing in.
error_message: HTTP 302 redirect to /login after successful authentication
symptoms: Credentials are accepted; browser receives a session cookie; subsequent request is treated as unauthenticated.
technician_notes: Inspected response headers and compared cookie domain and secure settings with the HTTPS deployment.
root_cause: The session cookie was configured for the old HTTP domain and was not sent to the HTTPS hostname.
solution: Updated the session cookie domain and secure settings, restarted the application, and verified a complete login flow.

title: PostgreSQL service starts slowly after reboot
description: The database host is reachable after reboot but PostgreSQL takes several minutes before accepting connections.
symptoms: Applications receive startup responses for several minutes; PostgreSQL logs show recovery processing; no new corruption is reported.
technician_notes: Reviewed PostgreSQL recovery logs and host shutdown history and confirmed the process was making progress.
root_cause: The host lost power during a write operation and PostgreSQL needed extended WAL recovery.
solution: Allowed recovery to complete, verified database consistency, and confirmed normal startup on a controlled restart.

title: Internal service unavailable after certificate renewal
description: An internal HTTPS service becomes unavailable immediately after its certificate is renewed.
symptoms: Nginx fails to reload; existing worker serves intermittent connections; certificate and private key do not match.
technician_notes: Validated the certificate and key pair using public metadata only and tested the Nginx configuration.
root_cause: The renewal process installed a certificate from a different request than the configured private key.
solution: Installed the matching approved certificate and key pair, validated Nginx, and completed a client HTTPS test.
